text.p: The following Australian economic indicators and events are scheduled for this week.
DAY GMT Indicator Period Forecast Previous
Thu 0030 Unemployment rate Oct 8.7 pct 8.7 pct
Possible 2230 Private sector credit Sep n/f +0.3 pct
Mon RBA governor Macfarlane at BIS meeting in Basle

EMPLOYMENT - Employment is expected to have bounced a little in October following September's steeper than expected 34,100 fall but not by enough to bring the unemployment rate down from 8.7 percent. That level has already been cited by the Reserve Bank as too high, so such a result will keep downward pressure on interest rates. The data may be useful in gauging the chance of another easing down the track, which analysts are believe is possible given the recent run of weak domestic data.
A soft employment outcome and a jobless rate at the psychological 9 percent level would certainly stoke speculation the easing cycle might encompass more than one cut.

Since the original survey last Friday, Bain revised down its forecast sharply Monday to -10,000/-20,000 from an original +20,000. "The softness in September retail trade data and the fall of seasonal influences on the labour market suggest to us that we will not see a rebound until November," Bain said of the revision. A weak 1.0 percent fall in October ANZ job ads figures, released earlier this week might also lead to downward revisions in expectations, Bain said. J.B.Were was the only other forecaster to cut its employment estimate, to -5,000 from +5,000. The revisions took the median employment growth estimate to +12,000 from +13,000.
